dvcat: a terminal UI for DVC

The problem it solves

DVC does its job, and its command line output is not friendly. Which stages are stale, and why? Did the parameters change, a dependency, the command or an output? What does the experiment table look like across five runs? The answers are there, but you have to piece them together from several commands.

The general idea

dvcat (DVC and cat) is a minimal terminal UI for DVC that I built in Rust with ratatui, in Catppuccin colours. It shows the pipeline, marks every stage as fresh or stale and tells you the reason, runs a stage with a live log you can cancel, draws the stage graph and has a table of experiments with deltas, a chart and actions to create, apply, remove or branch an experiment.

Examples

cargo install --git https://github.com/MarcellGranat/dvcat --locked

cd my-dvc-project
dvcat

The keys are the ones from the other terminal tools:

  • j/k move, Enter steps into a stage's files, o opens a file in the editor.
  • r runs the selected stage only, R runs it with its stale upstream stages, x cancels.
  • g shows the stage graph, e the experiments table with m for differences from the baseline, n for a new experiment.

Tips from my setup

  • Staleness with a reason. The stage detail says whether the parameters, the dependencies, the command or the outputs changed, and which parameter exactly. That is the view I missed most.
  • A run survives the UI. Quitting leaves a running stage running, and dvcat picks it up again when I open it in the project, which fits long runs on the computer at home. See the post about working from anywhere.
  • It finds DVC through the project. dvcat looks for the DVC of the project's virtual environment first, then for one on the path, so it works with the uv setup.
  • Built with agents and OpenSpec. The plan for each feature is an OpenSpec change in the repository, and a coding agent implemented it. See the posts about OpenSpec and my Claude setup.
  • A demo. just demo builds a small project with three experiments, so you can try everything without your own pipeline.
